parts.prompt:
Which property distinguishes a gas from a liquid?
A. Fills all available space
B. Occupies a measurable volume
C. Contains particles in motion
D. Has a measurable mass
parts.canonical_answer:
A. Fills all available space. A gas expands to fill its container; a liquid retains a fixed volume.
Distractor explanations: B: Liquids also occupy measurable volumes. C: Particles move in liquids as well as gases. D: Liquids also have measurable mass.
marking_guidance: Correct option A (1). A. Fills all available space. A gas expands to fill its container; a liquid retains a fixed volume. Distractor explanations: B: Liquids also occupy measurable volumes. C: Particles move in liquids as well as gases. D: Liquids also have measurable mass. No mark for more than one selected option.

parts.canonical_answer: A single series circuit connects supply, switch, ammeter and two separated graphite electrodes dipping into the sample. The sample completes the path between electrodes. See the labelled reference circuit in visuals/VIS-6117-2-circuit.svg.

Ammeter correctly in the path (1).

parts.prompt: Describe a method for comparing aqueous sodium chloride with sugar solution using the low-voltage apparatus. Include how the observations are recorded and how contamination between samples is reduced.
parts.canonical_answer: Test each solution with the same voltage, electrode spacing and immersion depth. Record the ammeter reading in a results table for each named sample. Switch off between tests and rinse electrodes with deionised water, removing residual rinse water before the next sample.
marking_guidance: Test the named solutions using the apparatus (1).
Record the ammeter reading against each sample in a table (1).
Rinse electrodes between samples to avoid contamination (1); switching off is required safe procedure.

parts.content_target: Compare conductivity and physical behaviour of ionic, molecular and metallic samples. Interpret and evaluate observations and experimental data.
parts.credit_requirement: Explain conductivity using mobile ions in solution (1), mobile electrons in metal (1), absence of mobile charges in a molecular sample (1).
parts.prompt: Explain these observations: a copper strip conducts; solid sodium chloride does not; aqueous sodium chloride conducts; sugar solution does not. Identify the charge carriers where present.
parts.canonical_answer: Copper conducts through mobile delocalised electrons. Aqueous sodium chloride conducts through mobile ions, whereas the ions in solid sodium chloride are fixed. Sugar dissolves as neutral molecules, so its solution has no appreciable concentration of mobile ions from the sugar and gives negligible current in this test.
marking_guidance: Mobile electrons in copper (1).
Mobile ions in aqueous NaCl, distinguished from fixed solid ions (1).
Neutral sugar molecules give no appreciable ionic conduction in this test (1).

parts.content_target: Compare conductivity and physical behaviour of ionic, molecular and metallic samples. Identify sources of error and suggest procedural improvements.
parts.credit_requirement: Describe controlling electrode spacing (1), immersion depth (1), and voltage (1) for a fair comparison.
parts.prompt: Describe improvements to this method: the electrode gap changes between solutions, immersion depth is not fixed, and the supply is changed from 3 V to 6 V for the second solution. Link each improvement to the comparison.
parts.canonical_answer: Fix electrode spacing with a holder so the current path length is comparable. Mark and maintain immersion depth so the electrode contact area is comparable. Keep the supply at 3 V so a changed driving voltage cannot explain the different response.
marking_guidance: Fixed spacing linked to comparable current path (1).
Fixed depth linked to comparable contact area (1).
Same 3 V supply linked to a fair electrical comparison (1).
